- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot after spikes.  
- If recent auction supply events are frequent and net supply is negative, model should not over-forecast upward; adjust downward bias if true outcome shows mean reversion.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >70), model should not continue rising; cap forecast at 1–2 price points above peak to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast magnitude; model should not ignore sentiment-driven downward pressure.  
- When official event balance is heavily bearish (net supply < -15) and true outcome is volatile, model should not assume linear trend; allow for mean reversion or volatility clustering.  
- If model forecasts are flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong upward movement, check if sentiment history includes recent bullish spikes — if so, adjust forecast upward with slight acceleration.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, consider reducing forecast slope or introducing early correction based on sentiment momentum.
